title: Fetch API
subtitle: fetch, JSON, REST API calls, error handling
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Websites need to load data without reloading the page — product listings, search results, user profiles, stock prices. Before Fetch (and XMLHttpRequest before it), this required verbose, error-prone code.
whyItExists.solution: The Fetch API is the modern browser standard for making HTTP requests. It returns Promises, integrates naturally with async/await, and handles all HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH).
whyItExists.whenToUse: Any time you need to communicate with a server or third-party API: loading data, submitting forms without page reload, sending analytics, real-time updates.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: For large-scale apps, consider axios (better error handling, interceptors, auto-JSON) or React Query/SWR (caching, loading states, refetching). Fetch is perfect for learning and small projects.

explainModes.beginner: fetch('/api/data') makes an HTTP request and returns a promise. Then you call .json() to parse the response into a JavaScript object. Use async/await to write it like normal code.
explainModes.simple: const res = await fetch(url) — res is a Response object. Check res.ok or res.status. await res.json() parses the JSON body. For POST: fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(data) }).
explainModes.standard: fetch() only rejects on network errors — HTTP errors like 404 or 500 still resolve. Always check response.ok. Headers are set in the options object. Credentials (cookies) require { credentials: 'include' }. AbortController cancels in-flight requests.
explainModes.technical: The Fetch API uses the Request, Response, and Headers objects. Response.body is a ReadableStream — for large responses, stream chunks with for await (const chunk of res.body). CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) controls which origins can fetch from a server — the server sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers. SameSite cookies and credentials work differently cross-origin.
explainModes.deepDive: The Fetch API is built on Service Workers — fetch events in a SW intercept all page requests for offline caching. The Cache API (caches.open, cache.put, cache.match) stores responses for offline use. Background Sync and Background Fetch APIs schedule fetch operations even after the page closes. The experimental Priority Hints API (fetchpriority attribute) and speculation rules API hint the browser about resource priority.

questions.question: When does fetch() throw an error?
options: Only on network failures (no internet, DNS error, CORS block)
When the response body is empty
questions.explanation: fetch() only throws on network failures. HTTP errors like 404 or 500 resolve normally — you must check response.ok or response.status manually and throw yourself.

questions.question: What does JSON.stringify() do in a POST request body?
options: Parses a JSON string into an object
Converts a JavaScript object into a JSON string for sending
questions.explanation: fetch's body must be a string (or FormData/Blob). JSON.stringify(obj) converts a JavaScript object to a JSON string. On the receiving end, JSON.parse() or response.json() converts it back.

faq.q: What is CORS and why does it block my fetch requests?
faq.a: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a browser security rule that blocks requests to a different domain unless the server explicitly allows it. If you see a CORS error, the server needs to add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers. You can't fix CORS on the client side — it must be configured on the server.

faq.q: What is the difference between fetch and axios?
faq.a: fetch is built-in (no install needed). axios auto-parses JSON, throws on HTTP errors, supports request cancellation, and has interceptors. For simple uses, fetch is fine. For production apps with auth, retries, and complex error handling, axios or React Query/SWR adds value.

examples: GitHub's web interface uses fetch to load PR diffs, comments, and file trees without page reload
Google Maps uses fetch to load map tiles and location data as you pan
Discord fetches message history when you scroll up in a channel
